record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: Establish the relationship between the sheaf R of Cauchy-Fueter regular functions and the sheaf B^Q of hyperfunction solutions to the operator or matrix Q arising from the syzygy complex. For n = 2, the matrices P and Q originate the sheaves of regular and anti-regular functions respectively; for n = 3 and higher, Q is no longer simple, although P and Q have the same characteristic variety.

evidence.quote: Problem: Establish a relationship between R and B^Q.
For n=3 the matrix Q is not so simple anymore, and in general we do not know the relationship between the sheaves R and B^Q.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions and consider $\mathbb{H}^n$ with coordinates $q_\ell = x_{0\ell} + i x_{1\ell} + j x_{2\ell} + k x_{3\ell}$, $\ell = 1,\dots,n$. The Cauchy–Fueter operator in the $\ell$-th variable is
$$\partial_\ell = \partial_{x_{0\ell}} + i\,\partial_{x_{1\ell}} + j\,\partial_{x_{2\ell}} + k\,\partial_{x_{3\ell}}.$$
A function $f:\Omega\subset\mathbb{H}^n\to\mathbb{H}$ is (left) Cauchy–Fueter regular if $\partial_\ell f = 0$ for all $\ell$. Writing the system in matrix form $P\,f=0$ where $P$ is the $n\times 1$ column of Fueter operators (after identifying $\mathbb{H}\cong\mathbb{R}^4$), one obtains a finite free resolution of the associated module over the polynomial ring $\mathbb{R}[x_{\mu\ell}]$:
$$0 \to F_N \xrightarrow{Q} F_{N-1} \to \cdots \to F_1 \xrightarrow{P} F_0,$$
in which $Q$ denotes the last (highest) syzygy matrix in the Cauchy–Fueter complex. Let $\mathcal{R}$ be the sheaf on $\mathbb{H}^n$ of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions (the sheaf of solutions of $P$), and let $\mathcal{B}^Q$ be the sheaf of hyperfunction solutions of the system defined by $Q$. For $n=2$, $Q$ is again a Cauchy–Fueter-type operator and $\mathcal{B}^Q$ may be identified with the sheaf of anti-regular hyperfunctions. For $n\ge 3$, $P$ and $Q$ have the same characteristic variety but $Q$ is no longer a simple Fueter-type operator.

Problem: For every $n\ge 2$, describe explicitly the relationship between the sheaves $\mathcal{R}$ and $\mathcal{B}^Q$ on $\mathbb{H}^n$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on hyperfunction sheaves arising from the syzygies of the Cauchy–Fueter complex in several quaternionic variables turn up surveys and resolutions that recall this question but do not provide a general description for $n\ge 3$. The matrix $Q$ becomes complicated beyond $n=2$, and no result identifying $\mathcal{R}$ with $\mathcal{B}^Q$ (or otherwise relating them) for general $n$ appears in the available literature; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems on the Analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter System in Several Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on the Cauchy-Fueter system, including the relation between the regular sheaf and the hyperfunction sheaf associated with the last syzygy.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of relating R and B^Q is stated as open in the survey.

status_evidence.title: Quaternionic and Clifford Analysis in Several Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses sheaf of regular functions and hyperfunctions in several quaternionic variables; for n=2 the last syzygy Q gives anti-regular functions, but no general description is provided for n>=3.
status_evidence.claim: No general identification of B^Q with R is given for n>=3.
